[p. 415]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah An-Nazi'at.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿By those who pull out violently﴾

The *waw* is for oath, and the thing sworn by is omitted. Its attributes were mentioned in all the subsequent items, up to His statement: ﴿And those who arrange affairs﴾ [an-Nazi'at 5].

Scholars have differed concerning what is sworn by in all of them, as will be explained, if Allah wills.

"An-nazi'at" is the plural of *nazi'ah*. *Naz'* is pulling a thing forcibly from its place, like pulling the bowstring from the bow's belly. It is used for both the tangible and the abstract. From the first kind is pulling the bowstring, as we have mentioned. From it is His statement: "and he drew out his hand" [al-A'raf 108]. Also His statement: ﴿It pulls people out as though they were trunks of uprooted palm trees﴾ [al-Qamar 20], and His statement: ﴿He stripped off from them their clothing﴾ [al-A'raf 27]. From the abstract kind is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾ [al-Hijr 47], and His statement: ﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾ [an-Nisa' 59]. And the hadith: "Perhaps a vein pulled it out" [i.e., the child was pulled from its place].

*Ighraq* means exaggeration, and *istighraq* means comprehensiveness.

As for what is meant by ﴿those who pull out violently﴾ here, scholars have differed about it, reaching about ten opinions. Among them: they are the angels who pull out souls; the stars that move from one place to another; the bows that pull arrows; the warriors who draw their bows; the warriors who set out from the land of Islam to the land of war for fighting; and wild animals that run toward the ṭalā, i.e., wild animals.

"An-nashitat": it was said the root of the word is *nashat*, meaning activity and lightness. *Unshuzah* is a knot that is easy to untie. *Nashshatahu* means he tied it, and *anshatahu* means he untied it quickly and lightly. From it is his statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "As if he had been released from a tether" (ﷺ).

As for what is meant by it here, scholars have differed about it in roughly the same manner as above. It was said: the angels gently take (*tanshut*) the souls. It was said: the souls of the believers are gently released at the time of terror. Ibn Jarir did not prefer any one of these meanings and said: all of them are possible. Others related all of them.

The Jalalayn mentioned only the first of these meanings. What the context and other texts support is that each of "an-nazi'at" and "an-nashitat" refers to the angels, and this is what was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid. They are attributes of the angels in taking souls.

The indication of the context for this meaning is that these are two contrasting attributes: the first is pulling with force, and the other is gentle release with lightness. So pulling with overwhelming force applies to the souls of the disbelievers, and gentle release with lightness applies to the souls of the believers. This has been explained in His statement, exalted is He, concerning the taking of the souls of the disbelievers: ﴿If only you could see the wrongdoers in the overwhelming agonies of death, while the angels extend their hands, [saying], "Release your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation"﴾ [al-An'am 93], and it continues.

• And His statement: ﴿If only you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs, [saying], "Taste the punishment of the burning"﴾ [al-Anfal 50]. And He said concerning the believers: ﴿O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr 27–28].

• And His statement: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised"﴾ [Fussilat 30].

This fits perfectly with the end of the surah before it, where He said: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment, the Day a man will look upon what his hands have sent forward﴾ [an-Naba' 40]. A man's looking at what his hands have sent forward begins from the state of pulling out, when the tongue becomes heavy in speaking during the death rattle, when repentance is no longer accepted at the moment of seeing what he is about to face. Then he looks at what his hands have sent forward at that time. This is at the pulling out of the soul or its gentle release. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By those that glide smoothly﴾ ﴿and those that race swiftly﴾

It has been said: "al-sabihat" (those that glide) are the stars. It has also been said: the sun, the moon, the night and the day, the clouds, the ships and the fish in the seas, and the horses on the racecourse.

Ibn Jarir also mentioned all of these without giving preference to any one of them. He said: "All of them are possible," and others mentioned them in the same way.

The reality is that all of them are great signs that point to His power, exalted is He. However, the context concerns the matter of resurrection and the return (to the Hereafter), and the closest of the cosmic signs to this context are: the sun, the moon, and the stars. Allah has described the sun and the moon as "swimming" (sabihat) in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day; each is travelling in an orbit (falak) they swim along﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]. And "those that race swiftly" (al-sabiqat) refers to the wandering stars (al-sayyarah, the planets).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then those who arrange an affair﴾

The exegetes (mufassirun) are agreed that they are the angels (mala'ika). Al-Fakhr al-Razi mentioned an opinion of his that is far-fetched, namely that they are the spirits (arwah), and that they may arrange a person's affair during sleep (manamat). This is a view upon which no reliance is placed, as you can see.

What the text supports is that they are the angels, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord, with every matter﴾ [al-Qadr: 4], and as Allah described the angels by His saying: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 6:

The saying of Allah Most High: ﴿On the Day when the Quaking (al-Rajifah) convulses,﴾ ﴿followed by the Following (al-Radifah).﴾

They are the two blasts in the Trumpet (al-Sur). The Rajifah is the first, and the Radifah is the second, as in the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.﴾ [Az-Zumar: 68].

Our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, had already discussed this in Surah Ya-Sin, at the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and behold, they will rush forth from their graves to their Lord.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 51]. The first is called al-Rajifah because of the intense quaking that seizes the whole world, as in the saying of Allah Most High: ﴿And the earth and the mountains will be lifted and crushed with a single crushing﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 14], and His saying: ﴿So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious﴾ [Az-Zumar: 68].

Ibn Kathir mentioned, from Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, with his chain of narration: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The Quaking came, followed by the Following; death came with what is in it." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think if I make all my prayer upon you?" He said: "Then Allah will suffice you for whatever concerns you of your worldly life and your Hereafter." And its chain: Ahmad said: Waki' related to us, Sufyan related to us, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Abu al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from his father, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said..." [the hadith].

(p-418) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "Shall we indeed be returned to our former state?"﴾ Ibn Kathir said: The polytheists deny resurrection after death, and "al-Hafirah" (the former state; lit. the hollow/track) is the life after their death and their going to the graves.

It is also reported that al-Hafirah means the Fire, but most of the exegetes hold that it is the first life. It is said: "He returned on his hafirah," meaning he went back along his path, as if his first life had dug out (hafara) his path by his walking in it. According to this, it has no connection with the hole (huffrah) of the grave; rather, it is an Arabic expression for returning to a matter. The poet's verse bears witness to this:

Shall I return to youth after baldness and gray hair? God forbid, from baldness and disgrace!

That is: shall I return to youth after baldness and gray hair?

And another's verse:

Advance, brother of Nahm, toward the bracelets (i.e., the battle);
And let not the heads of the (dead) fallen frighten you; they are scattered.
For your abode is only the dust of the one who keeps vigil (the grave),
Until after it you return to al-hafirah,
After you have become decayed, crumbling bones.

The verse that follows also shows that what is meant by al-hafirah is the return to life once more, in His saying: ﴿They say, "That would then be a losing return."﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 12]

Al-Karrah (the return) is the return to the first life, and it is what precedes the hole of the grave, namely the recurrence of the previous life. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Even when we are decayed bones?﴾ The "decayed bones" (al-ʿiẓām al-nakhira) are those that are rotted and through which the wind passes, as in the words of the poet:

؎I emptied them of their marrow, so they are like glass vessels, in whose hollows the wind whistles (tankhur).

The "nakhrat al-rih" (the nakhra of the wind) is the intensity of its sound, and from it comes "al-manakhir" (the nostrils), because air is taken in through them. What points to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he made for Us a parable and forgot his own creation. He said, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78].

**His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿Has there come to you the story of Moses?﴾

(p-419) Allah, exalted is He, explained this story, its subject matter, and its place by His saying after it: ﴿When his Lord called him in the sacred valley of Tuwa﴾ ﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed﴾, up to His saying ﴿And said, "I am your lord, the most high"﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 24].

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 79, verse 16:

Allah's statement, ﴿When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley﴾. The Noble Qur'an clarifies that this valley is al-Tur (the mountain), in His statement: ﴿So when Moses had fulfilled the term and set out with his family, he perceived from the side of the mount a fire﴾, up to His statement: ﴿So when he came to it, he was called from the right bank of the valley, in the blessed place﴾ [al-Qasas: 29-30]. The "blessed" (al-mubarakah) is equivalent to the "sacred" (al-muqaddas).

Thus Allah clarified that the calling took place at al-Tur, which is the sacred valley, and it is Tuwa, and it was in the blessed place. Allah has also clarified what took place in that place of intimate discourse (munajat), the matter of the staff, and the other signs, in Surah Ta-Ha, from the beginning of His statement: ﴿Has there reached you the story of Moses? When he saw a fire﴾, up to His statement: ﴿Go to Pharaoh﴾ [Ta-Ha: 9-24].

Our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, explained in detail the discussion of that station in Surah Maryam, at His statement: ﴿And We called to him from the right side of the mount﴾ [Maryam: 52].

In Surah Ta-Ha, Allah has clarified the complete account of the calling, from His statement: ﴿Indeed, I am your Lord, so take off your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa﴾. ﴿And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed﴾. ﴿Indeed, I am Allah; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance﴾. ﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming﴾ [Ta-Ha: 12-15].

Then (He clarified) the account of the staff and the sign in his hand, peace be upon him, and his being sent to Pharaoh, who had transgressed, and Moses' supplication: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, ﴿and ease for me my task﴾ [Ta-Ha: 25-26], and his asking that his brother be made his minister with him. This is without addressing the method of the call (da'wah). In this noble surah there is an explanation of the methodology of the call and what the Prophet of Allah, Moses, should be upon with the enemy of Allah, Pharaoh.

The manner of presentation is: ﴿Would you like to purify yourself? And I would guide you to your Lord so you would fear Him﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 18-19]. Then comes the presentation of the greatest sign and the evidence of the truth of his claim, which every caller today must stand before, since there is no one today more (arrogant) than Pharaoh, nor more tyrannical than him, for he claimed both lordship and divinity together, saying: ﴿I am your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 24], and he said: ﴿I do not know for you any deity other than me﴾ [al-Qasas: 38]. (p-420) And there is no one today more honored by Allah than the Prophet of Allah, Moses, and his brother Aaron.

Nevertheless, the methodology of the call is from the most noble of Allah's creation to the most disbelieving of Allah's servants, with this gentle, soft, and wise manner, proceeding from His statement: ﴿So speak to him with gentle speech; perhaps he may be reminded or fear﴾ [Ta-Ha: 44]. So they both did as Allah commanded them, and they spoke as Allah taught them: ﴿Would you like to purify yourself? And I would guide you to your Lord so you would fear Him﴾. This methodology is the realization of His statement: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction﴾ [al-Nahl: 125].

The Qur'an has laid down a complete methodology for the call to Allah, and the scholars have elaborated it with what is required of the caller and of the one called, and the consideration of the condition of the one called.

Our Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has also presented: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves; no one who has strayed can harm you once you are guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105], from Surah al-Ma'idah.

And His statement: ﴿And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you﴾ [Hud: 88], in Surah Hud.

And His statement: ﴿And argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl: 125], in Surah al-Nahl.

All of this together constitutes a complete methodology regarding the path of the call to Allah, the Exalted, concerning the caller, the one called, what he calls to, and the manner of doing so. And all praise is due to Allah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he showed him the greatest sign﴾ ﴿but he denied and disobeyed﴾

Here he mentions only "the greatest sign" (al-ayah al-kubra). And from it (i.e., from what Allah mentions) He, exalted is He, mentions that Pharaoh combined denial (al-takdhib) and disobedience (al-isyan). It has already been mentioned in Surat al-Qamar His saying: ﴿And warnings had certainly come to the people of Pharaoh﴾ ﴿They denied all of Our signs, so We seized them with the seizure of One Mighty and Able [to do all things]﴾ [al-Qamar: 41-42], and the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) has already explained that there.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 25:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah seized him as an example (nakal) for the Hereafter and the former life﴾

Al-nakal (exemplary punishment) is a name for that which is made a nakal (deterrent) for others, i.e., a punishment for him so that others take warning from it. The word derives from al-imtina' (refraining, holding back), and from it comes al-nukul 'an al-yamin (refusing to take an oath), and al-nakl (shackle). This is what al-Qurtubi said.

It has been disputed concerning "the Hereafter and the former": is it the [two states of] this world and the Hereafter? Or are they the two great statements which Pharaoh uttered in his saying: ﴿I know of no god for you other than myself﴾ [al-Qasas: 38]?

The second is his saying: ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 24].

Ibn 'Abbas said: "There were forty years between them." Ibn Kathir chose the first view, and Ibn Jarir chose the second, and many of the exegetes are with him.

However, an objection is raised against Ibn Kathir's choice: the context placed the Hereafter first, whereas the punishment of Pharaoh, in which the nakal of the former [life], which is this world, comes first.

Likewise, an objection is raised against Ibn Jarir's choice: Allah, exalted is He, made His seizing of him a nakal, so that whoever fears might take warning from it, and the lesson is stronger with what is perceptible, whereas his two statements were uttered in his own time.

The Qur'an bears witness to what Ibn Kathir said, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So today We will save you in your body, that you may be a sign to those who come after you﴾ [Yunus: 92], and this is the locus of taking warning.

Allah, exalted is He, also said after the verse: ﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 26].

The demonstrative in His saying "Indeed in that" refers to the seizing and the nakal mentioned, i.e., the verbal noun implied within His saying ﴿So Allah seized him﴾ and His saying "nakal". Rather, "nakal" is itself a verbal noun, meaning: Allah seized him and made an example of him, and made his nakal (exemplary punishment) a lesson for whoever fears.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 27:

Allah's statement: ﴿Are you the more difficult to create, or is it the sky He constructed?﴾

When Pharaoh was in that state of rebellion and disbelief, and among the causes of his rebellion were kingship and power, as in His statement: ﴿And Pharaoh, the lord of the stakes﴾ [al-Fajr: 10],

• and His statement: ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land﴾ [al-Qasas: 4],

• and His statement about him: ﴿Does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me, and these rivers flowing beneath me?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 51].

All of these are manifestations of his rebellion and factors of his strength. Allah addressed them with what this rebellion led to, then addressed them regarding themselves, warning against the rebellion of power: ﴿Are you the more difficult to create, or is it the sky?﴾, to the point that even if you claimed that you are stronger than Pharaoh, whom Allah seized with the punishment of the Hereafter and the former life, then are you the more difficult to create, or is it the sky?

The answer has come explicitly stating that the sky is more difficult to create than them, in His statement: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

He also showed the weakness of man in His statement, with the same meaning: ﴿So ask them: are they the more difficult to create, or those We have created? Indeed, We created them from sticky clay﴾ [al-Saffat: 11].

In this there is an indication of His power to resurrect them after their death and their becoming decayed bones.

Something of this was already mentioned by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, at the verse of "al-Saffat": ﴿So ask them: are they the more difficult to create, or those We have created?﴾ [al-Saffat: 11].

* *

Allah's statement: ﴿constructed it﴾ ﴿He raised its height and perfected it﴾

The explanation of this was already given by the Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, in Surah Qaf at His statement: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We constructed it...﴾ [Qaf: 6], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 79, verse 30 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the earth after that He spread out (dahaha)﴾ ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾ ﴿And the mountains He set firmly﴾.

In this noble verse the earth is described as "dahaha" (spread out) by God, may He be exalted. In another verse it is said that He "tahaha" (with the letter ṭāʾ), and in another verse that He spread it out, namely His saying: ﴿And at the earth, how it is spread out?﴾ [al-Ghashiyah: 20].

Scholars have differed concerning the interpretation of His saying "dahaha". Ibn Kathir said: its explanation is what follows it, ﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture﴾ ﴿And the mountains He set firmly﴾ [al-Naziʿat: 31-32], and this is the view of Ibn Jarir from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-Qurtubi said: "dahaha" means He spread it out.

The Arabs say: "daha al-shayʾ" when he spread it out.

Abu Hayyan said: "dahaha" means He spread it out and prepared it for dwelling and settling upon it. Then he explained that preparation by what is indispensable of bringing forth water and pasture, and setting the mountains firmly.

(p-423) From what has been mentioned, dwelling and livelihood are made possible, including salt, food and drink, and this is precisely the words of al-Zamakhshari.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: "dahaha" means He spread it out. Thus you see that nearly all the exegetes agree that "dahaha" means "spread it out".

The saying of Ibn Jarir and Ibn Kathir, that "dahaha" is explained by what follows it, does not conflict with spreading out and preparation, as Abu Hayyan said: it mentions the necessary requirements of settling for livelihood upon it, from bringing forth its water and pasture, because by these two the life is sustained.

Among what may be adduced in support is that "al-dahw" is known in the sense of spreading out, the saying of Ibn al-Rumi:

Never shall I forget a baker I passed by, who spreads the thin bread in the blink of an eye,
Between seeing it in his hand as a ball and seeing it as a round moon,
Only for the time that a circle ripples on the surface of the water when a stone is thrown into it.

Concerning this verse the question of the shape of the earth has been raised: is it flat or spherical and round?

When we return to the major books of lexicography, we find the following:

First: in al-Mufradat of al-Raghib: he said "dahaha" means he removed it from its place and its settled position.

From this are the expressions: "daha al-matar al-hasa ʿan wajh al-ard", meaning the rain swept the pebbles from the surface of the earth; and "marra al-faras yadhu dahwan", when the horse dragged its foreleg over the face of the ground so that it spread its dust.

From this also is "udhhiyy al-naʿam" (the ostrich's nest-scrape). He said: "al-tahw" is like "al-dahw", and it is the spreading out of a thing and its removal, and "al-ard wa ma tahaha" (the earth and what spread it). He cited the verse of the poet:

"Tahā bika qalbun fi al-hisan tarub"
meaning: a heart smitten with the beauties carried you away.

In Mu'jam Maqayis al-Lugha, the root d-ḥ-w: the dal, the ḥāʾ and the wāw are one root indicating spreading and preparing.
It is said: God dahā the earth, yadḥūhā dahwan, when He spread it out. It is said: the rain dahā the pebbles (p-424) from the surface of the earth, and this is because when it is so, it has prepared the earth.

It is said of a horse, when it throws its hand forward without lifting its hoof much from the ground: "marra yadhu dahwan". From the same root is "udhhiyy al-naʿam": the place where it lays its eggs, an "ufʿūl" form from "dahawtu", because it scrapes it with its leg and then lays eggs in it, and the ostrich has no nest.

In Lisan al-ʿArab, the root d-ḥ-a: al-dahw is spreading; "dahā al-ard yadhuwhā dahwan": he spread it out.

Al-Farra' said concerning His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And the earth after that He spread out (dahaha)﴾: he said, He spread it out, and he mentioned al-udhhiyy, the ostrich's egg-place in the sand, because the ostrich scrapes it with her leg, then lays eggs in it.

He mentioned the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar: "fa-daha al-sayl fihi bi-al-batha'", meaning: he threw and cast.

He said: Ibn al-Musayyab was asked about "al-dahw" with stones, and he said: there is no harm in it, meaning throwing them and racing.

From Ibn al-Aʿrabi: "huwa yadhu bi-al-hajar", meaning he throws it and pushes it. The "dahi" is the one who scrapes the stone with his hand. He recited for Aws ibn Hajar, in the sense of "yanziʿu" (plucks):

"Yanziʿu jild al-hasa ajashshu mubtarik, ka-annahu fahisun aw laʿibun dahin."

In the hadith of Abu Rafiʿ: "I used to play with al-Hasan and al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them both, with al-madahi." These are stones like a small disc; they would dig a hole and scrape with those stones, and if the stone fell into it, its owner won; if it did not fall, he lost.

And al-dahw is the throwing of the player with a stone, a nut, or other things. End quote.

What the author of al-Lisan mentioned from Abu Rafiʿ still exists today in Medina, and it is called al-dahl with the lām, just as it was described exactly.

After presenting the statements of the principal lexicographical sources and what has preceded from the statements of the exegetes, we confront the dispute between some scholars of astronomy (al-hayʾa) and other scholars concerning the shape of the earth, and perhaps, by a favour from God, we will be granted success in clarifying the truth in this matter, so that no one supposes a contradiction between the Qur'an and what is established from the sciences of astronomy, and so that no ignorant person is deceived by what is said in Islam.

(p-425) On reflecting on the statements of the exegetes, we find them agreeing in their totality that "dahaha" means He prepared it and made life upon it easy, and mentioned the requirements of enabling life upon it: bringing forth water and pasture, and placing the mountains. This agrees with the texts of the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place?﴾ ﴿And the mountains as pegs?﴾ [al-Naba': 6-7].

And His saying: ﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its broad paths and eat of His provision﴾ [al-Mulk: 15].

All of this belongs to one category, namely its preparation and the enabling of living upon it, and there is in it no meaning of rounding or circularity.

When we come to the books of lexicography, we find them all explicitly stating that "dahw" is spreading, throwing, removal, and preparation. Spreading, preparation, and throwing a round stone into a small hole are shared meanings, and all of them interpret "dahaha" as meaning He spread it out and prepared it. And that "udhhiyyah" is the ostrich's egg-place, not its egg, as they say, and it is so called because she scrapes it with her foot in order to lay eggs in it, since she has no nest.

Accordingly, there is no proof from the books of lexicography that "dahw" means "takwir" (rounding). But what is the view of the scholars regarding the shape of the earth, setting aside whether the Qur'an addresses it or does not address it?

When we return to the words of Muslims who have examined the science of astronomy, we find them agreed that the shape of the earth is round.

Before quoting some of their statements, we alert that this research has no connection to the subject of motion, whether of the earth or of other things; that is a separate investigation, not its place. Rather, the discussion here concerns shape.

As for the statements of scholars regarding the shape of the earth, the most comprehensive, explicit, and clear of what I have come across is the speech of Ibn Taymiyyah in Risalat al-Hilal. In it he said at one point: "It has been established by the Book, the Sunnah and the consensus of the scholars of the Ummah that the celestial spheres are round. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon﴾ [Fussilat: 37], and He said: ﴿And He it is who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; each in an orbit they swim﴾ [al-Anbiya': 33], and God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each in an orbit they swim﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]."

(p-426) Ibn ʿAbbas said: "in a whorl like the whorl of a spindle." Thus it is in Lisan al-ʿArab: al-falak is a rounded thing; from it one says: "tafallaka thady al-jariya" when a girl's breast became round. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ [al-Zumar: 5]. And "takwir" is "tadwir" (rounding). From it it is said: "kara al-ʿimama wa kawwaraha" (he wound the turban and rounded it). For this reason the celestial spheres are described as having a round shape, because the origin of "kurah" (ball) is "kurwah", the waw moved and the letter before it was open, so it was changed to an alif.

He said: ﴿The sun and the moon are by a reckoning﴾ [al-Rahman: 5], like the reckoning of the millstone; and He said: ﴿You see no disparity in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Mulk: 3]. This happens only in shapes that are round, not in polygons of triangles, squares or others, for these are uneven, since their angles differ from their right angles. A round body is uniform in its sides and directions; no part of it differs from another.

He also said in it: Al-Imam Abu al-Husayn Ahmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Munadi, one of the notable scholars known for knowledge of traditions and great compositions, in the foundational texts of religious sciences, of the second generation of the companions of Ahmad, said: There is no disagreement among scholars that the heaven is like the shape of a sphere, and that it turns with all the stars in it, like the turning of a sphere upon two fixed poles that do not move, one of them in the north and the other in the south.

He said: What indicates this is that all the stars revolve from the east, falling slightly, in one order in their movement and in the proportions of their parts, until they reach the middle of the sky, then they descend in that same order; so they seem fixed in a sphere that turns them all in one revolution.

This is a sampling of the statements of Muslim scholars on the shape of the heavenly spheres. Then he said: This is the principal aim, and likewise they agreed that the earth with all its motions, of land and sea, is like a sphere.

He said: What indicates this is that the sun, the moon and the stars do not rise and set simultaneously for all who are in the various regions of the earth, but rise first in the east before the west.

He said: Thus the earth is fixed in the middle of the sphere of the heaven, like a point in a circle. This is indicated by the fact that the body of each star is seen in all regions of the sky at one size, which indicates that the distance between the heaven and the earth in all directions is one measure; so it is necessary that the earth be at the centre of the sky. End quote, in his exact words.

This is a transmission of the consensus of the Ummah from a great imam in both rational and transmitted sciences, that the earth is shaped like a sphere, and he adduced the compelling proofs from the motion of the spheres for this.

Also from the standpoint of reason it is said: the most perfect of bodies is the round one, as he said in His saying: ﴿You see no disparity in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Mulk: 3].

Accordingly, if a traveller were to walk on the surface of the earth, and we supposed the earth flat like the surface of a house or a sheet of paper for example, this traveller would have an end he reaches, which is the limit of the flatness, or he would fall into an abyss. But if it is taken as a sphere, he completes his circuit and returns again; and if he travelled his whole life, his journey would have no end, because he moves over its surface in all its directions. And God knows best.

Note.

It would have been possible to present this conclusion from the outset, since it agrees in the end with the statement of the scientists of astronomy, and we would not prolong the quotations from here and there. But we have adduced all of that for a more general purpose than all this, and a more comprehensive question, which concerns two aspects:

The first: that Muslim scholars were aware of what the astronomers said, but not through transmission or a specific indication of this part of the Qur'an, rather through reflection and inference; for the Muslim scholars were not ignorant of this theory, and this truth was not hidden from them.

The second: despite their knowledge of this truth and their grasp of this theory, not one of them claimed that its indication applies to the texts of the Book or the Sunnah.

On this basis we say: if the texts are not explicit regarding a modern theory, it is not proper to force them into its discussions, whether in denial or affirmation; rather we seek knowledge through its proper path. The sciences of astronomy proceed by reasoning and inference, the sciences of medicine by experiment and induction. Thus the Qur'an remains protected from the arena of dispute over a theory capable of being established, negated, or changed and replaced. Likewise, one who does not know the reality of a matter in its field should not hasten to deny it, unless it contradicts an explicit text.

[p-428] It is incumbent upon him to verify first. We have already drawn attention to this earlier, in a similar case: the story of Allah's Prophet Sulayman (Solomon) with Bilqis (the Queen of Sheba) and the hoopoe (al-Hudhud) when it came to him. It said: ﴿I have encompassed what you have not encompassed, and I have brought to you certain news from Sheba﴾ [al-Naml 27:22], and it related to him the account of her and her people. Peace be upon him did not rush to deny it because the one who brought the report was a hoopoe, nor did he know anything about it. Nor did he hasten to affirm it, because he had no basis for it. Rather, he took the path of verification by means of the same channel through which the report had come to him. He said: ﴿We shall see whether you have told the truth or were among the liars﴾ [al-Naml 27:27], and he sent him with a letter to them. If this was the conduct of Allah's Prophet Sulayman, who had means and capabilities as you know, then others are even more deserving of it.

Another admonition.

If the scholars of Islam affirm the sphericity (kurawiyyah) of the earth, what do they say about His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Do they not look at the camels, how they were created? ... and at the earth, how it was spread out?﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:17-20]? Their answer is like their answer concerning His words, Exalted is He: ﴿until, when he reached the setting place of the sun, he found it setting in a murky spring﴾ [al-Kahf 18:86], meaning from the viewpoint of the eye. For the sun sets over one nation and remains visible over the horizon of another nation, until it reaches its rising place from the east on the morning of the following day. The spreading and levelling of the earth is considered with respect to each region and part of it, given its vastness and the greatness of its mass.

This does not contradict the reality of its shape. We see a towering mountain, and when we climb it and reach its summit, we find a level plateau, and we find a community with all its necessities, though some of its inhabitants may not know about the rest of the world, and so on. And Allah knows best.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab [Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book]):

[p-432] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Nazi'at

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And the earth, after that He spread it out﴾.

The way of reconciling this with His words: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days... then He turned to the heaven﴾ [Fussilat 41:9-11], has already been discussed in Surat al-Baqarah, in the commentary on His words, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth, then He turned to the heaven﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:29] and the verse that follows it.

The author said in (Dafʿ Iham al-Idtirab ʿan Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾.

The way of reconciling this with the verses that indicate the generality of warning, such as His saying: ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [25:1], in Surat Ya-Sin and elsewhere, has already been explained.

The verse says: ﴿As if they, on the day they see it, had not remained but an evening or its morning.﴾ Al-'Ashiyyah is the period from the decline of the sun (zawal) until sunset, and al-Duha is the period from sunrise until the decline of the sun. This is a delimitation by half a day.

The delimitation by an hour of the day has also occurred. And there is: ﴿a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Baqarah: 259]. And there is: ﴿You did not remain except ten [nights]﴾ [Yunus: 103].

The explanation of this was already given by the Shaykh, may God's mercy be upon us and upon him, at his words in Surah (p-429) Yunus: ﴿And [mention] the day He will gather them, [and it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day﴾ [Yunus: 45]. He referred there to the removal of the appearance of contradiction from the verses of the Book, and it will be published, God willing, together with this supplement.
